new_value: {"notes":"Implemented in git-vouch: History/registry_history (linear order = git rev-list --topo-order --reverse HEAD; working tree is one pending version at index final; a non-git dir has only that version, so plain-dir tests keep snapshot semantics). check_registry: tier record judged by approver's claimed+valid tier at the commit that added its current content (History.added), recursion ends because claimed rank strictly falls; tier record committed before its person file -\u003e void (warning); key in two files -\u003e first listing commit owns, later lister is an error and dropped, same-commit ties keep the old current-key rule; every revocation version ever committed counts, processed in commit order, signer eligibility (key itself, subject's and anchors' unretired keys) taken from files at that commit, void if signer revoked in a strictly earlier commit, same-commit revocations all count; CheckResult gains warnings (revoked key still current). Errors only for working-tree versions; historical bad versions are silent. Tests: tests/test_check_history.py (13 tests, real git + ssh-keygen; snapshot-copy cross-checks). Open question: automation accountable still judged at the current tree (accountable stepping down = error)."}

new_value: {"notes":"Implemented in git-vouch: History/registry_history. Positions = git rev-list --topo-order --reverse --parents HEAD plus the working tree (final); ORDER IS ANCESTRY (History.before/concurrent, one ancestor bitset per commit), never the topo index, because merge shape is author-controlled. Merges that kept one parent's content are added as versions (git log --merges -m, blobs via read_blobs, factored out of file_history) so History.at is exact; History.added traces such merges back to the commits that introduced the content (tuple; two branches can add the same bytes). check_registry: tier record valid if approver may grant at every adding commit AND no concurrent commit lowered the approver's authority (error otherwise); before-person-file -\u003e void; automation accountable must be maintainer/anchor at the adding commit (error) and have a valid tier at the tree (void otherwise, vouch-ey47.16). Key ownership: first listing over every person-file version in history, by ancestry; tied (same commit or concurrent) -\u003e current-key rule. Revocations: key must be owned by the subject, signer keys owned by their lister; void only if the signer was revoked in an ancestor commit; concurrent/same-commit count (vouch-ey47.17); rejected historical revocations are warnings. Review round 1 (7 findings) all fixed; tests in tests/test_check_history.py (22, real git + ssh-keygen), each fix mutation-checked. Open questions: vouch-ey47.16, .17, .18."}
